title: Session reset if idle or off screen for long time
body:
If I leave an active session open on a tab and come back to it later, the connection re-establishes, but it is a new session. 
I work in Byobu (Screen/tmux) so I don't lose my session, but I have to re-open it to continue working. 

Sessions that were not in Byobu are lost and I can see the new connection on the same terminal.
author: LeonvanHeerden

title: Roles and Scoping
body:
Not that there isn't already enough in front of you, but was thinking of a roles and scoping kind of feature.

This way if one or more users login, you can set permissions on a folder or it not a folder on a group of connections. Then set who can see them etc.

Ultimately, this would result in a user logging in, but cannot see the passwords and connection details of the server, but can still use and connect to the servers you allow them.

So it would be object permissions like Read, Edit, Delete associated to a role like Helpdesk Technicians
Then scoping that created role over one or more connections, or groups of connections.
author: freedbygrace

comments.body: In the newest version of Termix this has slightly been implemented. Users can create hosts, save them to their account, and then share the host with another user, allowing them to only connect but not edit the host, and see sensitive information. However, you have brought up many interesting features that I could definitely see me implementing in the future.

title: password is saved/displayed in docker log - this is a security risk
body: As title, this is not good practice, the password should not in a log file in plain text.
author: simowilso

comments.body: Haha, yeah maybe that was not my smartest move. In the next update Il have that fixed and hopefully revamp the logging system including moving a lot of the UI logging to that such as the connected to ssh text that appears when connecting to a host. Thanks!

I agree, but in the meantime, you can disable logging while you get it running without issues. I added this to my Docker Compose file:

```yaml
services:
  app:
    logging:
      driver: none
```
or
```yaml
services:
  app:
    attach: false
This issue has been fixed and resolved in the new version 1.1 update that has just been released.
